topSignals.title: DOE meets Trump's July 4 nuclear goal: three microreactors achieve zero-power criticality
topSignals.text: — The U.S. DOE confirmed on July 1 that Deployable Energy's Unity reactor achieved criticality at Idaho National Laboratory (June 30, 11:55 PM MDT), fulfilling EO 14301's mandate for three reactors to go critical before July 4. Preceding it: Antares Nuclear's Mark-0 (June 4, INL — first under DOE pilot programme) and Valar Atomics' Ward 250 (June 18, Orangeville, Utah — first criticality outside a national lab). All three are zero-power test reactors; none sells a watt of electricity. For SOFC competitive assessment: nuclear remains a 2030+ threat, not a near-term data center power competitor. Radiant (Kaleidos) did not achieve criticality by the deadline but is cited as next in queue. Forbes | World Nuclear News | Energy News Beat

topSignals.title: UBS and Evercore ISI both raise Bloom Energy PT to $350 on $25B Brookfield catalyst
topSignals.text: — On July 1, UBS analyst Manav Gupta maintained Buy and raised the Bloom Energy price target to $350 from $322, and Evercore ISI analyst Nicholas Amicucci raised to $350 from $295 (Outperform). Clear Street also moved to $290 from $250. BE closed July 2 at ~$299.71 (range $283.50–$303.90), consolidating ~15% below the new dual target while the market awaits Q2 earnings July 30 (consensus: ~$820M revenue, ~34% gross margin, EPS ~$0.39). July 3 is a shortened session (markets close 1pm ET pre-Independence Day). GuruFocus / UBS | GuruFocus / Evercore | Investing.com

topSignals.title: FuelCell Energy slides from +67% peak as warrant dilution and negative margins draw scrutiny
topSignals.text: — After the +67% weekly rally (June 26–July 1), FCEL pulled back on July 2 ("sliding Thursday," Benzinga). Seeking Alpha published a Sell note ("What Goes Up Must Always Come Back Down") flagging: 34% share count dilution in two quarters, persistent negative margins, and the Fit Energy 12M-warrant overhang (12M shares at $26.44 strike). The counter-thesis: FCEL cannot self-fund its $200–275M Torrington expansion; sustained dilution erodes the upside of the data center bull case. Benzinga | Seeking Alpha | ts2.tech warrant analysis

items.text: EFCF 17th European SOFC & SOE Forum closes today (July 3, Lucerne) — Final day of the conference. Technical paper sessions ran July 1–3 at KKL Lucerne; no specific experimental results have been published online as of this digest. Proceedings will appear on efcf.com; watch for post-conference press releases from Elcogen (E3000 G2 real-stack efficiency and degradation), Ceres licensees (Doosan yield ramp), SolydEra, and Convion. Key pending data: (a) Elcogen E3000 G2 efficiency at real commercial conditions (stated 75% electrical / 90% with heat, 650°C), (b) any confirmed degradation benchmarks from Doosan (last known: 80% production yield vs. 90% target in Q1 2026), (c) manufacturing cost per kW from ELCO I Tallinn vs. Bloom Fremont baseline. EFCF

Three US microreactors reach zero-power criticality by July 4 deadline — See Top Signal #1. The milestone fulfils EO 14301 symbolically and accelerates federal attention on advanced nuclear. But the reactors — Antares Mark-0, Valar Ward 250, and Deployable Energy Unity — are zero-power research demonstrators. No commercial power dispatch capacity exists; commercialisation timelines for AI data center applications remain 2030+ at earliest. The headline risk for SOFC is narrative (increased investor interest in nuclear) rather than operational (nuclear cannot absorb data center load before 2030). Forbes | Power Magazine / Antares

Background: Microsoft Project Kilby (2.67 GW CCGT, Texas, first power 2028), DOE $17.5B AP1000 nuclear loan programme (10+ year horizon), Google Meitner Energy Center (wind/solar/battery + gas firming) — all covered June 27–28.

Bloom Energy (BE) — July 2 close: ~$299.71 (range $283.50–$303.90). Updated analyst picture post-$25B Brookfield deal: UBS Buy $350 (raised from $322 on July 1), Evercore ISI Outperform $350 (raised from $295 on July 1), Clear Street $290 (raised from $250), Barclays Equal Weight $276. BE trades ~15% below the new dual $350 targets; gap to close likely requires Q2 earnings confirmation on July 30. 52-week range: $21.50–$351.28. GuruFocus | Blockonomi | MarketScreener

FuelCell Energy (FCEL) — Pulling back from +67% weekly run. July 2 decline attributed to warrant dilution concerns and Seeking Alpha Sell note. Full analyst picture: B. Riley Buy $32 (Street high), Jefferies Buy $24, UBS Neutral $22. Next catalyst: Q3 FY2026 earnings ~September 2026. Benzinga | Seeking Alpha

EFCF proceedings: not yet published — Final conference day today. Proceedings expected post-July 3 on efcf.com. Watch press release channels for Elcogen, Ceres Power, and SolydEra for post-EFCF announcements. Key pending item: Elcogen E3000 G2 real-stack efficiency and degradation data; any confirmation of >=75% electrical / >=90% CHP at 650 degrees C at commercial scale would be a material LCOE model input. EFCF

NASA regenerative fuel cell system tests (Glenn Research Center, February 2026) — NASA Glenn is testing an H2/O2 regenerative fuel cell (not SOFC) for Artemis lunar power. The system functions as both generator and electrolyser to cycle water on the Moon. Not directly relevant to data center SOFC, but validates fuel cell durability for high-uptime extreme environments; Bloom H2-capable servers have been flagged as a candidate for off-grid remote power applications. NASA Glenn | Simply Wall St

lcoe.text: Nuclear criticality milestone — no LCOE impact before 2030: the three DOE Pilot Programme reactors are zero-power demonstrators. Commercial AI data center nuclear power remains 2030+ in any realistic scenario. Do not adjust near-term SOFC LCOE competitive assumptions on this milestone.

Dual analyst convergence at BE $350: UBS and Evercore ISI converging at $350 on the same day establishes a new sell-side consensus ceiling. If Bloom discloses manufacturing cost-per-kW progress on July 30, update the LCOE capex assumption accordingly — especially the 2027 downside scenario (~$4,000/kW post-ramp).

FCEL dilution risk: if Torrington expansion financing stalls (dilution concerns, negative margins), MCFC competitive pressure in the 1–50 MW data center segment may be delayed beyond late 2027. Maintain SOFC (Bloom) as the dominant near-term supply assumption in LCOE scenarios.

Watch post-EFCF announcements (next week): if Elcogen E3000 G2 commercial-conditions efficiency is confirmed at >=75% electrical / >=90% CHP at 650 degrees C, update BOP cost assumptions for 650 degrees C-class systems — potentially $500–1,000/kW below 800 degrees C alternatives. No data yet.
